self-effacing

self-uh-FAY-sing · adjective

What It Means

Self-effacing is modest and reluctant to draw attention to oneself or one's achievements.

The self-effacing scientist credited her entire lab, not herself, when accepting the award.

Example

Despite writing a bestselling book, the self-effacing author still described herself as 'just someone who got lucky.'

Self-effacing describes a genuine reluctance to accept praise or draw attention to one's own achievements.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unassuming: Unassuming means not showy and not demanding special treatment -- an unassuming manner, an unassuming little house. Self-effacing is more active: a self-effacing person does not just skip the show, she steers attention and credit away from herself and hands them to others.

humble: Humble describes how you rate yourself on the inside -- believing you are no more important than anyone else. Self-effacing describes what you do on the outside: deflecting attention and passing credit away. A person can feel humble and still accept the spotlight; a self-effacing one steps out of it.

reserved: Reserved means keeping your thoughts and feelings to yourself -- saying little and showing less. Self-effacing is not about silence: a self-effacing speaker may chat warmly all evening, so long as she keeps turning the spotlight away from herself. Reserved hides the person; self-effacing hides only the credit.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

boastful: showing excessive pride in one's achievements

arrogant: having an inflated sense of one's own importance

Where it sits · how actively attention is avoided — modest → self-effacing → retiring

modest vs. self-effacing: Modest is the everyday word for downplaying one's achievements; self-effacing goes further, actively avoiding attention or credit.

retiring vs. self-effacing: A retiring person goes even further than self-effacing -- not just waving praise away but shrinking from notice altogether, happiest out of the room when the applause starts.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Self-effacing is a compound of 'self' and 'effacing' (from efface, 'to rub out or erase'), literally describing someone who tries to erase their own presence from the spotlight.

Use the root in a new word: deface

Use the root in a new word: deface: Deface comes from the same Latin root facies ('face') buried inside efface, though deface means to spoil the surface of something, quite different from self-effacing's modest retreat from attention.

Self-effacing is almost always a compliment, though taken too far it can also read as false modesty.
